target: Persist the human operator's 2026-08-14 ten-ADR ACCEPT dispositions into repository authority as ten new accepted ADR records under docs/90-adr/, an acceptance head, an operator decision ledger, an acceptance binding and an acceptance receipt. Purely additive: it touches nothing the merged Second Brain contract validator reads, so that validator stays at 94 checks / 0 failed. It starts no implementation, authorizes no runtime, and creates no enablement claim.
invariants: RISK_LANE=L2. Authority persistence only; no runtime, no implementation.
HUMAN_GATE=PASSED. ADR-SB-001..010 = ACCEPTED_BY_OPERATOR, ten explicit per-ADR rows supplied 2026-08-14, not a bulk token and not inherited.
MA08_MAIN_SHA=75b4cfc581786a53445e412bfc8e25a6e0fdb978, re-verified unmoved immediately before persisting. The Phase B MA-08 result NO_NEW_MATERIAL_DRIFT therefore still binds.

PERSISTENCE IS ADDITIVE. The following are READ-ONLY and any write to them fails the packet: the candidate document (validator A35, and it is sha-pinned authority), fo-01-repair-status.json (B02/B03/B05/B06/B07), FO01_RESOLUTION_RECEIPT.json (B05/B07, and another packet's historical audit record), schemas/second_brain/contracts/** (A34/A36/A37), scripts/governance/validate_second_brain_adr_contracts.py, and docs/03-reference/architecture/second-brain/authority/**.

The validator must report PASS_SECOND_BRAIN_ADR_MACHINE_CONTRACT_COVERAGE with 94 checks and 0 failures BOTH before and after persistence. A drop is a packet failure, not an expected consequence of acceptance.

The ten accepted records are GENERATED from the amended candidate bytes at CANDIDATE_SHA256 by a committed generator. Nothing is salvaged from the superseded attempt at 19fa74faa9, whose records carry the pre-amendment AC#2.

The generator fails closed: it refuses to run unless the candidate hash matches, the amended AC#2 appears exactly ten times, the pre-amendment AC#2 appears nowhere, and the candidate is still CANDIDATE.
Every decision section in every accepted record is a byte-slice of the candidate. No section is paraphrased.
Each accepted record states on its face that acceptance confers no implementation, runtime, production or enablement authority, preserving acceptance condition #3 into the accepted form.

The three fo-01-repair-status.json fields that this persistence makes stale are DECLARED BY NAME in ADR_ACCEPTANCE_BINDING.json. Silently leaving them, or silently editing them, are both packet failures.
SB-DEC-001..032 are not reopened; SB-DEC-026 remains A_LEAVE_UNLINKED; the ratification binding and the 32-decision operator ledger are unmodified.

Per the merged supersession lineage, only an independently audited rebuilt acceptance chain may become authoritative. This packet is therefore not complete until a fresh independent audit of its own frozen head returns 0 blockers and 0 must-fix.

steps.task: Re-verify origin/main is unmoved and map the validator's constraints before writing anything.
requirements: origin/main is re-read from a fresh fetch and must still equal MA08_MAIN_SHA, or an MA-08 delta addendum is required first.
Every validator guard that enforces 'no ADR is accepted' is read from source and recorded, so the additive design is deliberate rather than lucky.
commands: git fetch origin --prune && git rev-parse origin/main
validation: The validator's full read surface is enumerated and shown not to include docs/90-adr/.

steps.task: Generate the ten accepted ADR records from the amended candidate bytes.
requirements: The generator is committed and deterministic.
It fails closed on candidate hash mismatch, on the pre-amendment AC#2 being present, on the amended AC#2 not appearing exactly ten times, and on the candidate no longer being CANDIDATE.
One documented slug rule is applied to all ten; no slug is hand-shortened.
Every emitted decision section is verified to be a substring of the candidate after writing.
validation: Ten files emitted, each status: accepted.
Each carries the amended AC#2 and none carries the pre-amendment wording.
Each decision body is a candidate byte-slice.
The full docs hook gauntlet passes on all ten.

steps.task: Emit the acceptance records and index rows.
requirements: The index generator is idempotent and never double-appends a row.
The ledger carries the operator's verbatim election and stated reasoning, with facilitator_authored_dispositions false and inheritance from 19fa74faa9 explicitly false.
The binding declares by name every fo-01-repair-status.json field this persistence makes stale, and states why it is not fixed here.
validation: Ten index rows added on first run, zero on re-run.
Ledger parses and records ten ACCEPT dispositions.
Binding names three stale fields and two that are not stale.

steps.task: Prove the persistence was additive, then freeze.
requirements: The validator reports 94/0 after persistence, as it did before.
Every changed path is inside the union of this packet's allowlist and its predecessors', verified programmatically.
No read-only surface appears in the diff.
validation: zero changed paths outside the allowlist union.
zero read-only surfaces in the diff.

steps.task: Fresh independent audit of the frozen persistence head.
requirements: Required by the merged supersession lineage, which states that only an independently audited rebuilt acceptance chain may become authoritative.
The prompt is authored after the freeze and names the head it audits.
The verdict is recorded verbatim; a FAIL or a remaining must-fix stops the packet.
commands: grok --cwd <throwaway worktree at the frozen head> -m grok-4.5 --always-approve --output-format plain -p "$(cat <the audit prompt>)"
validation: BLOCKERS 0 and MUST_FIX 0 on the controlling round.
The auditor confirms no read-only surface was written.
The auditor confirms the accepted records derive from the amended candidate and not from 19fa74faa9.

requirements: Nothing is pushed, no PR is opened, no implementation begins.

commit.allowlist_note: The last entry is an operator-authorized append-only correction record, written as a sibling to the merged record whose reasoning it corrects. It is listed here so that changed-paths remains a subset of the allowlist union; without it the correction would be an uncovered path, which is exactly what a commit allowlist exists to catch. The record it corrects was re-hashed after writing and is byte-identical.
